headline: Southborough advanced a $38 million Neary School renovation plan and saw voters divide on housing and trail funding at Special Town Meeting.
synopsis: October was highlighted by the Special Town Meeting, where voters authorized Community Preservation Act funding for a Peninsula Trail footbridge and golf course irrigation while defeating a two-family zoning amendment. Following that defeat, the Affordable Housing Trust moved forward with a separate draft amendment to eliminate Southborough's 7 percent cap on age-restricted senior housing developments. Meanwhile, the Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance schematic designs for a $38 million addition and renovation of Neary Elementary School after determining that a $15 million baseline repair option was not viable. Town officials also turned attention to FY28 budget planning, reviewing $2.15 million in capital requests while confronting an anticipated $2 million operating deficit. In addition, the Planning Board extended its review of the proposed Route 9 Costco project into December, and the Select Board urged state legislators to enact special legislation making the town clerk an appointed position.

top_items.title: Elementary School Building Committee advances $38M Neary renovation plan
top_items.why: The committee voted 4-0 to advance Option 3 into schematic design after architects demonstrated that a $15 million upgrade yields only $5.8 million in direct repairs.
top_items.body: Architectural reviews revealed that a $15 million baseline upgrade would largely be consumed by soft costs, contingencies, and mandatory code requirements such as fire sprinklers and accessibility compliance, leaving primary heating, univent, and educational upgrades unfunded without qualifying for state reimbursement. The committee authorized Tappé Architects to proceed with schematic designs, site evaluations, and detailed cost models for a $38 million addition and renovation ahead of an anticipated vote at the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Special Town Meeting rejects two-family dwelling zoning amendment
top_items.why: The proposal to ease restrictions on two-family home conversions earned an 85-80 majority at Special Town Meeting but fell short of the required two-thirds threshold.
top_items.body: Following the vote, both the Zoning Board of Appeals and the Affordable Housing Trust reviewed the results. Rather than revising the bylaw for the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting, the Zoning Board reached consensus to pause local action and wait for pending state legislation that could permit two-family housing by right.

top_items.title: Affordable Housing Trust advances senior housing bylaw update
top_items.why: The trust agreed on draft zoning language to eliminate Southborough's 7 percent townwide cap on age-restricted 55-plus housing units.
top_items.body: Because Southborough has reached its cap on age-restricted units, new senior developments are currently blocked. The trust endorsed Option 2, establishing a two-acre minimum lot size, an eight-unit-per-acre density limit, and a 12.5 percent affordable unit mandate. Members plan to present the proposal to the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Select Board ahead of a future Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Town Meeting approves CPA funds for Peninsula Trail footbridge
top_items.why: Special Town Meeting approved Article 4, granting up to $428,550 in Community Preservation Act funding to construct a pedestrian bridge along the Peninsula Trail.
top_items.body: Prior to Town Meeting, the Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to keep the full appropriation on the warrant despite negative recommendation votes from the Select Board and Advisory Committee. With funding approved, the Trails Committee is coordinating roadway crossing safety on Central Street and Route 30 with the DPW and MassDOT while preparing a 2027 MassTrails grant application to offset town expenses.

top_items.title: Committees review FY28 capital requests and operating deficit scenarios
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee evaluated $2.15 million in capital appropriations and up to $49 million in bondable projects against a projected $2 million town operating deficit.
top_items.body: Submissions are dominated by school, Public Works, and public safety needs, prompting the committee to schedule joint sessions with the Select Board and Advisory Committee. Department heads have prepared level-funded and service-reduction models in the event a Proposition 2 1/2 override fails, while the Regional School District is modeling scenarios and anticipating an $800,000 drop in regional debt service after FY27 as 2004 renovation bonds expire.

top_items.title: Planning Board extends Costco review deadline to December
top_items.why: The Planning Board continued the major site plan and special permit hearings for 21 Coslin Drive to November 2 and extended its decision deadline to December 18, 2026.
top_items.body: Board discussions continue to center on regional traffic impacts along Route 9, with the town awaiting completed consultant peer reviews. In related developments, the governor signed special legislation authorizing Southborough to grant an off-premises alcohol license for the proposed Costco warehouse through October 2028.

top_items.title: Select Board urges legislature to approve appointed Town Clerk
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to ask state Representative Kate Donaghue to expedite a home rule petition converting the town clerk from an elected to an appointed position.
top_items.body: Town Meeting previously approved changing the position to an appointed role, and board members emphasized the timing is urgent ahead of upcoming municipal election cycles. The office is currently filled by interim clerk Amy Berry, whose appointment runs through May 2027.
